utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- would be of some concern to you.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. In fact, we see that in Iraq. When they drafted the new constitution I believe it was the Shiite that wanted one person, one vote; 60 per cent, they win every time. They can appoint all the posts. But here in Bosnia, which was sort of a microcosm of Yugoslavia in a sense, it was multi-ethnic, you had three constituent peoples, Muslim, Croat, and the Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in Yugoslavia you had many more than --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Many more, yeah.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bosnia but those were overwhelmingly the three.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you had others as well?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But by and large and we need to make a distinction here, as you well know, between a constituent peoples and, say, a national minority. You're shaking your head again. We've got to make the record.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say -- would it be fair to say that all three sides were cognisant of this?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cognisant of the fact that they were each a constituent people?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And at least with respect to the Croats, they wanted equal share in governance along with the Muslims and the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not say they wanted an equal share in all cases. They wanted certainly a respectable share, but equal is a mathematical term and it wouldn't be safe to apply that to every Croat action.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Okay. Now, I look at -- I've looked at some of these agreements, and we're going to go through some of them starting with Cutileiro, and at no time do I -- do I see anything but the Croats asking to have their rights within, within a state government of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Decentralised but nonetheless within Bosnia-Herzegovina. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that would not be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because you have not mentioned the creation of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're going to get to that.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, but you asked a question and I think I have to answer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Well, Herceg-Bosna, I'll ask -- I'll jump ahead of schedule. Do you see any document in Herceg-Bosna that does not have on top Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't vouch for that. I haven't seen every document --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- issued by Herceg-Bosna, but it would not be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would not be unusual --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you by?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- to have a piece of paper that across the top said Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I can cite you an example for you, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me just go step-by-step. Now, I know you're not a -- you're not a lawyer and you were involved in -- in the big picture issues, but did you by any chance, you or your staff, I don't know whether you had a staff, it's not mentioned in your notes, but did you or any of your staff ever look at any of the legislation that was put in place by Herceg-Bosna to see what exactly is this Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had very good lawyers attached to the delegation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And are there --

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a have, very active staff. There were military advisors --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- And lawyers from the United Nations and other --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Entities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: So they did the looking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But did you actually ever sit down and read, for instance, the statutory decision that established Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did at some point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I don't want to go into -- too deep into this subject because I don't have the time, but is it fair to say that when the JNA attacked Croatia it's quite well known and we've heard testimony here that the JNA was staging the attack, some of the attacks against Croatia on territory belonging to Bosnia-Herzegovina? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not the main thrust of the JNA attacks. The Eastern Slavonia came right from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I didn't ask whether it was the main, but nonetheless it was being used. There's a point that I'm trying to get to.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been a staging ground, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are you aware that prior to the JNA moving -- moving towards B and H, that the Croats were asking the central government, such as it was at the time, to ready itself against this impending threat? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You must have heard the reaction from the Croats when -- and they often quote Izetbegovic who said this is not our war in reaction to what happened in -- in Ravno; correct?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Ravno.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ravno.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Were you aware of that? Ravno was razed basically by the JNA in BiH, and Izetbegovic, and he might have been misquoted but nonetheless it's out there in the public domain that "this is not our war" because at the time Izetbegovic is on the fence. He's waiting to see, is Croatia going to win or Serbia going to win or Yugoslavia going to win. So at that point in time he's not taking a position but the Croats are looking at the president of the Presidency and they're starting to wonder, who is this person and how can he protect our vital national interests if that's his position? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we did -- yes, we dealt a lot with President Izetbegovic, and his style was not precise at any point. He tended to wander off onto extraneous issues, and he -- he was a bright man. He spoke English like President Tudjman, but his -- his style of discussion and action was -- was somewhat ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Lacking?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't -- the word that comes to mind is dreamy, but I don't want to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- denigrate him. But it was rather loose and imprecise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, he was the head of the SDA was he not?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The SDA was the predominant Muslim party at the time in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. At this time while he's holding this, he's being the president of the Presidency and promoting himself as the president of this government, of BiH, actually. He's actually really the head of the Muslim party which had an agenda, did it not? And you told us what the agenda was earlier.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I've also said that he acted on behalf of the Muslims the way Mile Akmadzic, who was also in the government, acted on behalf of the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But at some point for all intents and purposes and I think we had a small snippet in one of your notes today, and I think this was an observation that you made, I could be wrong, that, you know, that there is no real central government. It's a fig leaf or something like that?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So for all intents and purposes -- I'm sorry to the interpreters. For all intents and purposes we have no central government, and what you have in Bosnia-Herzegovina are three groups of people that are -- that have organised themselves and a civil war going on.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not quite right. We had a central government that was recognised, and if you give me 30 seconds, I would call your attention to paragraph 11 of my statement, and I'd like just to read three or four lines because that answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 11. "Because of the" -- I'm reading from my statement. Paragraph 11. "Because of the military conflict, the Bosnian government in Sarajevo laboured under extremely onerous conditions: Sarajevo was besieged by the Bosnian Serb army and subjected to daily shelling; the Bosnian Serb army controlled approximately 70 per cent of the territory of BiH. Therefore, the powers as well as the activities of the government were severely limited." I think that answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you would read the rest of it because I think it helps round this topic up.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine, I'm happy to read it. "It was clear to the negotiators during the lengthy negotiations that President Izetbegovic, Silajdzic, and Akmadzic were representing the government officially, while Izetbegovic and Silajdzic were mainly representing Bosnian Muslim interests and Akmadzic was mainly representing Bosnian Croat interests."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I think that's -- pretty much is the case; right?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, there had been some complaints, had there not been, by the Croats that actually they were being disenfranchised at the Presidency or at the state level?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is only that one about the rotation of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I --

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could finish, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Go ahead. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And President Tudjman dealt with that and we dealt with it here. They had their own community. You see here they created the community of Herceg-Bosna and as far as the Bosnian Croats, that was the government. That was their government and it was it the government, just the way the Bosnian Serbs felt and said, "We have Republika Srpska; Dr. Radovan Karadzic is our president."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And in -- for all intents and purposes you had Izetbegovic with his community, and he's wearing two hats. One, he is the president of -- for the Muslims, by the Muslims, of the Muslims, and at the same time he's going around pretending to be the president of the entire country.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't pretending to be the president. He was the president, and he spoke -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He made very clear in his imprecise way on many occasions discussing the economy, for example, food supplies, refugees. We weren't always talking about the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And he made clear and indicated and indeed was the representative of -- of all of the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me -- let me just throw this out at you: Did you by any chance examine this concept called the Presidency? We don't have it in the States. When we think of the president we think of the commander-in-chief, the chief, the top executive who is going to run everything. But he was the president of the Presidency. Were you aware that he only had one vote and he was basically first among equals but that's all he was? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had read the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the last one that was extant. The Presidency consisted of nine people, three Serbs, three Muslims, three Croats, with one additional person who represented the group called "others," sometimes Yugoslavs. They used the term interchangeably. And you see by that it's self-evident this was the tie-breaking -- expected to be the tie-breaking votes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the Presidency was to rotate among the three parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Now the -- the others -- the person filling that other seat, that was Mr. Ganic, was it not?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And he's a Muslim, is he not?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But he was representing himself to be a Yugoslav, which at some point Yugoslavia ceased to exist so he could not have been a Yugoslav. He would have been one of the three -- one of the three constituent peoples. Anyway, were you aware that the president cannot make decisions on his own? In other words, it is the Presidency that makes the decisions? They have to vote on it. So in other words, he cannot act independently on his own.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. In peacetime that probably would have been the case, but this -- there was an armed conflict occurring at this time, and naturally in a situation like that people assume positions and powers that one would not find in peacetime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see that in the United States today, and the United States has -- a highly developed --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- country.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But -- I'm getting notes from my colleague that I should be in the constitution, and I think that's self-evident; right?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No. But what I'm saying is that assuming that you are correct, the powers that he would have taken on himself, those powers would have been -- the constitution would have allowed Izetbegovic to take on those powers; right?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was -- it was expected in -- as in any country that there would be consultations and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah, but sir, what I'm saying is this: You have a constitution. Usually the contusion provides for emergency situations. If, however, there is an emergency situation and the -- and the president decides to take power unto himself in disregard of the constitution, that's an unconstitutional act, is it not?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be if it were a clear case, as you describe it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah. And naturally others would not appreciate that unconstitutional act.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if -- if it were unconstitutional.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- they might object to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I don't want to debate the point at this point because we'll deal with this with other witnesses. Cutileiro. According to you, this is from your notebooks, on 18 April 1992, I believe you folks are in Lisbon, this is on page 113 of Exhibit 159. I'll just read it real quickly. You have a note that says that Cutileiro says, "It's absurd to blame BH exclusively on Serbs. Responsibility of all parties. Can be seen in -- at firsthand in tripartite talks." Then this goes on -- then in your notes you say apparently what Cutileiro said, "Izetbegovic is 'a liar', very untrustworthy. Always go back -- always goes back as to what he has to agree to." Now, do you recall writing that down?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have it in my handwriting in front of you, I wrote it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Cutileiro, he was a distinguished individual, was he not?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Portuguese diplomat, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, okay, you can be a Portuguese diplomat and still be distinguished; right?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. He was a former ambassador.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And did you have many dealings with him?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You indicated that he also wrote a book that you read.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now here he's calling Izetbegovic a liar back in 18 April, 1992, and I take it that has to do something with the -- the agreement that -- that Izetbegovic had signed and then had reneged and had pulled off his signature; correct?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That irritated quite a few people.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, for instance -- and I mean this is a hypothetical, of course, but had he kept the signature, no telling what might have happened, because the signature is on 18 March 1992. The Serbs had signed on, the Croats had signed on, and certainly this statement of principles did not call for the carve-up of Bosnia-Herzegovina, no telling whether the war could have stopped there at that point in time; right?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, it did call for the carve-up of Bosnia-Herzegovina into three sub-entities, a Muslim, a Croat, and a Serb. That was the essence of the Cutileiro Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was did within the context of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean within the territory of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Within -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It didn't call for three distinct countries?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please make pauses between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now perhaps we can just look at it real quickly. It's on map 10, Your Honours. Please. All right. Now, if we can all look at map 10. This is the map that was provided by the Prosecution. I believe it's Exhibit P 9276. It's multicoloured, and -- and so this is what the Cutileiro Plan called for; right?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a notional map. I must tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no definitive map ever developed by Cutileiro.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. But if you look at -- but this is -- you say it's a notional map. This is the Prosecution's map that they prepared. This is from March 1992, okay, but basically if we look at Cutileiro and we look at the plan carefully, it guarantees the rights of all the constituent peoples; right?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say the map guarantees rights; a map only draws lines on the earth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, but -- well, we don't see three distinct states, as you put it, number one. From the map it's self-evident.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that's precisely the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But -- but if you look at the statement of principles itself, it never called for these states to be independent of the state; correct?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- the Bosnian Serbs spoke about the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to focus you on the statement itself. You were very good with the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which statement are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The statement of principles, the March 18 statement of principles for the new constitutional arrangement for Bosnia-Herzegovina. Perhaps we can just look at 1D 0398. This is the -- in essence what Izetbegovic signed and withdrew his signature from. I think you called it the Sarajevo agreement in --

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I see it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It should be -- it was provided to you. Perhaps we can have the usher help us out here. But you may have it as well in front of you but it's buried among all those our documents, and I apologise. This is --

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, have you looked at this before? Have you seen this?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I don't want to belabour the point, but it talks about -- we can see in the -- that the editor -- editor's note says that it was subsequently repudiated by the Bosnian Presidency, the signature you verified, others verified, so there's no -- there's no dispute that Izetbegovic first signed and then withdrew his signature, but this lays out basically the vision as was seen -- and by the way, Cutileiro, was he speaking for himself or was he speaking on behalf of an institution?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was working for Lord Carrington. His function was a sub-function of the conference on Yugoslavia that Lord Carrington shared when the fighting began in March in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Lord Carrington asked Ambassador Cutileiro to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To do just that as a sub-unit of his conference. So, yes, he was working for Lord Carrington and the conference on Yugoslavia and the EC.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactly. That's the whole point. Okay. So he carried some weight. I mean, he wasn't just somebody who was there volunteering?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, no, this was an official negotiation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we look at this, it says, just on the first paragraph, which is independence, Bosnia-Herzegovina would be a state composed of three constituent units based on national principles and taking account economic, geographic, and other criteria.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Go ahead and comment.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll be brief. That illustrates the point I made to you earlier. There were to be three states within a state composed of three constituent units, a Bosnian Serb state, a Bosnian Croat state, a Bosnian Muslim state, based on the national principles. In other words, ethnicity and religion were to be the decisive factors. They were to be the foundation of the state. It states that clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If you go on, and we don't have time, but the Judges are jurists and can read the document and we will -- obviously we will bring others to comment on it as well, but wasn't one of the missions that Cutileiro had was to make sure that all the constituent peoples were -- their rights were protected within the state called Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, indeed, just as we had that responsibilities. So Ambassador Cutileiro --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- would have had that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, it doesn't call for ethnic cleansing, in other words, or movement of population. It doesn't call for that.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Transfer or ethnic cleansing is not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nor would I expects it to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Nor -- nor was it envisaged, was it?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know. I was not active in March 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, sir, obviously --

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pardon me, March 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You can't -- you can't -- seriously, you can't tell us that Mr. Cutileiro, Ambassador Cutileiro and others would have envisaged or would have expected or would have condoned any movement of population or any ethnic cleansing be it direct or indirect in drafting such a plan they were promoting in order to bring peace to this very volatile situation? You're not stating that, are you?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your are asking me to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You can't answer that question. Very well. All right.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because even if -- if I may finish the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because even if that was not in the mind of Ambassador Cutileiro, it could have been, as you asked me, in the minds of others. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, that was a criticism also, as I understand it, of the Vance-Owen Plan. I'm not suggesting that there were others. There were some folks in the media who wanted to distance themselves or wanted to make sure that the Vance-Owen Plan did not succeed, and they were openly saying in the press that it would promote ethnic cleansing or movement of -- of populations.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was heavy criticism in the Vance-Owen Plan but that was not one of them. The criticisms that were false, the false criticisms of the Vance-Owen Plan were basically that it legitimised ethnic lensing that had already taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that it rewarded aggression, quote unquote. It rewarded aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Those, those --

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were the main criticisms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But those --

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And they were not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactly. Exactly. But going back -- one last point going back to Cutileiro -- and incidentally who came up with this nominal map, if you know?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you I spoke with Cutileiro on numerous occasions about the map and indeed I spoke with his legal advisor, Mr. Henri Darwin on precisely this point. And they both confirmed to me that there was no definitive map. There was a map, perhaps, but nothing definitive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But somebody must have sat down and prepared this?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If we could just look at it just very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, that's map 10, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if you could just briefly comment does this look like the Banovina to you, as you had described it? Because if I look at it, it certainly doesn't reflect the Banovina, and this is something that the Croats signed.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you look at it, you see in the north, in the Posavina at the top of where the border is Croatia, Posavina, Bosanski Brod, Odzak [phoen], Bosanski Samac, and Orasje, those were Croat areas and Croat and the bottom area, Herzegovina --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It doesn't look like Banovina, does --

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does. It does. It certainly does to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's don't like the ban convenient it certainly does to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not completely the banovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Nothing in your conversation with Mr. Cutileiro to suggest that it was the Croats that drafted this, came up with this -- that came up with this map?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was never agreed, as I've said a few times. Forgive me for repeating it. There was no definitive map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Right.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was never a definitive map of the Cutileiro.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But the but the Croats signed this, did they not?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know did they.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me -- well, maybe I can ask a couple more questions on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Incidentally, preceding, just to make sure that we understand one point, preceding this, the Cutileiro Plan there was a European Community conference and there was a draft convention, and I have here a treaty provision for the convention of 4 November 1991. This would be 1D 00893. Were you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir. Could you help us out here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You have it in your bundle but ti might be easier or quicker.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We wish to thank the ushers for helping us out. Now, did you see this document at all?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are you -- is there a problem, if The Prosecution are saying they didn't get it? Okay. We apologise to the Prosecution. We were told that maybe the -- maybe the gentleman gave it -- gave both copies to the witness. But this has been introduced before. But have you seen this before, sir?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have seen it in November 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in essence, you know, prior to Cutileiro the EC was trying to figure out an arrangement on how these republics could become independent.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already referred you to the conference on Yugoslavia chaired by Lord Carrington which began in July 1991 and continued until August 1992. It dealt with the entire country, that is the six republics, and it -- the goal was to either allow them to stay together or to separate peacefully if that was what they wished. That was Lord Carrington's goal. All six republics attended the meetings, and not this document but the one of October 18th is the definitive document. It's the treaty that Carrington laid down called, Arrangements for a Peaceful Settlement. You can get it on the UN document, October 18, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this is a gloss on that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But the point I wanted to make and I want to focus our Trial Bench to is that it was well thought out as to what rights, what human rights --

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- would be available or mandatory for the citizens of each republic, be they a national minority or a constituent peoples; right?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And it's fair to say that Cutileiro then, in drafting the Cutileiro Plan, would have had that in mind and would have been cognisant of those principles in crafting an agreement; correct?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to a point, because the situation in Bosnia, which was what Cutileiro was dealing with, the situation in Bosnia was entirely peaceful in November 1991, but by November 1992 there was a war on in Bosnia. So it was -- it was no longer the same situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But what I'm talking about are the principles, the human rights principles, making -- you know, that's what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the general principles on the -- if one looks at them, I see here human rights, following human rights the right to life, the right not to be subjected to torture, the right not to be subjected to slavery. Yes, of course he would not favour torture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I guess we'll leave with this last question, and that is that these principles never shifted, these human rights principles never shifted irrespective of whether when the drafting began or when the principles were set out it was peacetime and now you have war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the principles were the same. We're talking about human rights principles.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The principles remain the same. The observance might be different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree. Okay, we'll have to pick this up tomorrow when we're both fresher. Thank you very, very much, and I know it's very taxing to be here answering questions at this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, thank you. See you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. We shall resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 4th day of April, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.01 p.m.,
